1.title: Stromal vesicle transfer reshapes fibroblast heterogeneity in pancreatic tumors
1.method: Twelve synthetic donor samples were dissociated using the tumor digestion protocol and processed for single-cell RNA sequencing. Libraries were prepared with a droplet-based platform targeting 10,000 cells per sample. Reads were aligned to a reference transcriptome, and cells with fewer than 500 detected genes or more than 15 percent mitochondrial reads were excluded. Clustering used a shared nearest-neighbour graph at resolution 0.6. Vesicles were isolated by differential ultracentrifugation and applied to cultured fibroblasts at three doses for 48 hours. 2.title: Macrophage polarization in response to tumor-derived extracellular vesicles
2.method: Primary macrophages were differentiated from monocytes over seven days and exposed to vesicle preparations at 10 micrograms per mL. Surface markers were measured by flow cytometry at 6, 24, 48, and 72 hours using a nine-colour panel. Gating was performed on singlet, viable, lineage-positive events. SYNTHETIC SAMPLE DATA. 3.title: A benchmark of vesicle isolation methods for downstream proteomic analysis
3.method: Conditioned media from a single large culture batch was split three ways and processed by differential ultracentrifugation, size exclusion chromatography, and polymer precipitation. Each preparation was characterized by nanoparticle tracking analysis and analyzed by mass spectrometry in technical triplicate. SYNTHETIC SAMPLE DATA. This paper does not exist.
3.result: Ultracentrifugation produced the highest ratio of vesicle markers to serum contaminants but recovered roughly 40 percent of the particle count obtained by polymer precipitation. Size exclusion chromatography fell between the two on both measures. Protein identification depth was highest for polymer precipitation and largely reflected co-isolated serum proteins. 4.title: Computational deconvolution of stromal composition from bulk RNA sequencing
4.method: A reference signature matrix was constructed from single-cell profiles of matched samples. Synthetic mixtures of known composition were generated by pooling single-cell profiles at defined proportions. Estimation accuracy was evaluated against held-out mixtures using root mean squared error and Pearson correlation. SYNTHETIC SAMPLE DATA. This paper does not exist.

5.method: Vesicle preparations from three independent isolations were aliquoted and subjected to zero through five freeze-thaw cycles between minus 80 C and room temperature.
